  - region "Simple English explanation of Domain and Range":
    - paragraph: In simple English
    - heading "Understand Domain and Range" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "The domain is the allowed input set and the range is the output set. 1/(x−2) has domain x≠2, y=x² has range [0,∞), and √(x−3) has domain [3,∞). A useful rule is Domain and range: domain = allowed x, range = possible y. You can learn Domain and Range by trying one small example instead of long theory."
    - paragraph: "Ban zeros of denominators, keep even-root insides ≥0, then read the resulting y-values for the range. Example: Find domain and range of y=sqrt(x). The square root needs x >= 0. Square-root outputs are not negative. So the answer is domain x>=0, range y>=0."
    - paragraph: "In real life, trip time: Negative time is not allowed. Watch out: Reading range from horizontal values. Range is the set of y-values."
    - complementary:
      - generic: Try this example
      - paragraph: Find domain and range of y=sqrt(x).
      - generic "Compare your answer"
